scope: The historic Red Monastery church at Sohag in May 2024, including its tapered brick shell, two rows of arched recesses, roofless nave, eastern sanctuary and adjacent medieval keep.

primaryWrittenSources.facts: The Ministry identifies the surviving church and southern fortifications, and records the keep’s four levels with fired brick below and mud brick above.
Conservation director Elizabeth Bolman documents the lost medieval nave roof, surviving outer wall, two sculpted portals, south tower and enclosed three-apse sanctuary.
ARCE documents limestone paving, two restored granite columns in the nave, three sanctuary recesses, and a cross over the sanctuary dome.

Somers Clarke’s published 1912 survey describes exterior wall batter, small stone cornice blocks, two tiers of window recesses, rectangular portals on both long walls, and three conches under the square lantern.
